messages:
lena: FYI ran a focused microbench on the new KV interleaving + attention-kernel routing. Saw a noticeable regression on T4 when interleaved is enabled by default.

ramon: numbers?

lena: quick summary of the test setup and results:
- workload: chat-like (seq=1536, batch=8, gen=512)
- model: 7B-style, fp16
- separate KV + fused-flash: 82ms/token
- interleaved KV (same config): 118ms/token (+44%)

oli: that's large. Which kernel path did selector pick?

lena: selector preferred paged-fused variant (paged_fused_attn_v2) for interleaved because of the row-stride pattern. Profiler snippet:
```
SM occupancy: 70%
L2 read BW: baseline 190 GB/s -> interleaved 310 GB/s
DRAM write BW: 46 -> 88 GB/s
L2 miss ratio: 0.11 -> 0.34
chosen kernel: paged_fused_attn_v2
```

ciara: was dtype fp16 contiguous or packed? packing could change effective stride.

lena: fp16 contiguous. We tried int8 (dynamic) too; that flipped selector back to fused-flash for some shapes and reduced interleaved perf to 92ms/token (still ~12% worse than separate). Int8 has QAT/quality tradeoffs.

benchbot: automated run summary attached:
```
bench: kv_layout_interleave_test
node: t4-8
median(ms/token): separate 82, interleaved_fp16 118, interleaved_int8 92
note: interleaved increases L2 th by ~63%
```

ramon: two mitigations: (A) make selector prefer fused-flash on T4 for interleaved unless stride aligned; (B) change allocator to round per-row stride to 128 bytes.

oli: prefer quick selector change today, allocator change has memory hit. Can we detect at load time and consult perf DB for L2 counters to pick kernel?

lena: prototype heuristic I pushed locally: if layout==interleaved && (stride_bytes % 128) != 0 && hw.family==Turing && seq>=512 then force fused-flash. Pseudo:
```
if (kv.layout==Interleaved && (kv.stride_bytes % 128)!=0 && hw.is_turing() && seq>=512) {
  selector.force("fused_flash_v3");
}
```
I also added kv_layout tests that simulate misaligned base addresses.

ciara: allocator rounding reduces the L2 misses but costs ~2-4% memory overhead. For Dedicated customers with strict caps that could be problematic.

oli: memory vs perf trade -- product should weigh. Meanwhile, batcher-level policy could help: prefer separate KV for low-batch/latency-sensitive, interleaved for high-batch throughput (esp on A100).

lena: ran mixed-batch experiments: batch<4 separate wins for latency; batch>=8 interleaved wins on A100. So batcher-aware heuristic makes sense.

ramon: action items:
- lena: open selector patch PR with tests and smoke perf checks
- ciara: run allocator-rounding prototype on dedicated subset and report memory delta
- oli: update perf DB to include L2 counters per-shape so selector can consult historical data
- benchbot: add nightly regression for interleaved toggle

benchbot: created ticket INF-2387 and scheduled cron job 03:00 UTC

lena: rolled selector patch to hosted canary. Preliminary canary numbers (one run): interleaved_fp16 (canary) -> 86ms/token p50, p95=140ms, p99=220ms; separate baseline -> 82ms/token p50, p95=125ms, p99=200ms

ciara: that looks acceptable on canary. Keep dedicated memory analysis before making interleaved default globally.

lena: will update INF-2387 with allocator mem delta, perf traces, and regression graphs.
